post.title: A Look Into My Open GL Game Engine
post.description: I go in-depth in the features and other cool stuff Implemented into my engine!

content.p: Shadow rendering was an interesting challenge, to achieve this, I had to render depth from a directiional lights point of view and then apply a transformation in-shader projected into the main cameras point of view. By doing this I can calculate which areas are in shadow relative to the main camera and which are not.

I also integrated deffered rendering, this can allow me to add 100+ lights into the scene each affecting models individually, this also allows me more in-depth control over the rendering pipeline and allows for custom effects to be passed in between texture passes
These objects being rendered are also being rendered instanced so its a few draw calls instead of thousends, doing this improve performance of the application thoroughly

One thing I found annoying about the process was the implementation of new shaders, they would need a .vert component and a .frag component.
To solve this, I solution i came up with was to combine them into a single .shader file which contained both a .vert and .frag component

In order to be able to to this, I append a define into the shader which the program then can check what define is currently being written in order to compile either the .vert or .frag component, This helped keep my project clean and tidy and avoided unnecessary extra files.
